ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts 2236–2244 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, as amended (name clearance, registration, ultimate beneficiary disclosure).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of status / certificate of good standing of the corporate general partner (and any corporate limited partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registries (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, HKCRA, Companies Registry of the relevant jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for countries party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian diplomatic or consular representative in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Quebec registered office/service agent and the individual authorized to execute name-reservation and registration filings with the Registraire des entreprises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner's board of directors or sole proprietor (for a natural-person general partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (same as above; if executed in a non-Hague jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement and the proposed declaration of creation (déclaration de constitution) of the société en commandite
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec legal counsel or notary after execution, or a foreign notary if signed outside Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notarial certification or Hague Apostille (if signed in a Hague State); consular legalization for non-Hague signatures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport/identity copies of all individual ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the limited partnership, together with proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence, plus a competent authority for apostille/consular certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification; for non-Hague countries, Consular Legalization by the Canadian embassy or consulate having consular jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Name reservation certificate issued by the Registraire des entreprises following the online NUANS-equivalent name search in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required — domestic official document issued directly by the Quebec Registrar

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, directors, officers, authorized signatories and agents against: (i) Canada's Consolidated Autonomic Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (ii) the OFAC SDN List; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) designated terrorist entities listed pursuant to the Criminal Code; (v) global Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases utilising a risk-based approach aligned with World-Check/Dow Jones/Refinitiv data. Initial screening must be completed before the declaration of creation is filed; ongoing re-screening occurs every 90 days and on any change in ownership or control. All screening decisions must be logged with supporting search evidence and retained for a minimum of five years following termination of the business relationship or the end of a transaction as required by the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), any enterprise name in Quebec must have a French version that is legible and distinctive. Names submitted in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet using standard pinyin/romanization; the legal element must appear as 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in all public filings. The Registrar requires that the French name be the primary registered name, and any English or other-language trade names must be declared and displayed with the French version. Generic and descriptive technical terms (e.g., 'AI', 'LLM', 'API') will be accepted if accompanied by a sufficiently distinctive element (e.g., invented word or name).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gouvernement / Government of Canada or Quebec
Avocat / Notaire / Médecin / Ingénieur / Comptable professionnel
Fonds / Fund (when implying a regulated investment fund)
Any term that falsely suggests a connection to a professional order, the State, the Crown, or a regulated financial activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a name-rejection notice, the applicant may, within 30 days, file a written administrative response with the Registraire des entreprises, proposing alternative names or submitting evidence of distinctiveness (e.g., registered trademark certificate, consent letters from the holder of a conflicting name, NUANS search results). The Registrar will issue a final decision. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 30 days of the final decision. Name reservations may be renewed by an additional 90-day period prior to expiry, after which the name returns to the general pool.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical head-office address in Quebec is mandatory and must be capable of receiving service of process. A virtual office arrangement consisting only of a mail-forwarding P.O. box does not meet the statutory requirement. However, a registered agent can provide a real physical office address (e.g., a law firm's business-lobby facility) where notices can be served and staff are available during normal business hours; this arrangement is accepted for a passive limited partnership. For an active AI/LLM API platform, a co-working space or a dedicated operational office is recommended; a home office that is physically occupied and identifiable may also be accepted. Use of a strictly virtual suite without local personnel materially increases the risk of administrative rejection or deregistration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5%–15% annual probability for an AI/LLM API company with standard Stripe payment rails and no direct handling of virtual currency. The inspection probability rises to 20%–30% if the partnership directly accepts cryptocurrency (USDC) or operates as a money-services business requiring FINTRAC registration; in such cases the Registrar and FINTRAC may conduct unannounced on-site examinations. If a purely virtual office (no physical reception or local staff) is used, the likelihood of a Registrar inspection or a compliance challenge increases to approximately 25%–40% given the entity's modern digital-only profile.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2209-2262 (société en commandite / limited partnership), supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 27 and 33-40, on registration of the declaration of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), within the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None required. Quebec law does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for limited partnerships; contributions are contractually fixed in the partnership agreement and may be monetary or in kind. No escrow account is mandated, but the general partner must maintain a contribution receipt in the partnership books (Civil Code of Québec, art. 2236).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Custom Trust & Corporate Institute Limited Partnership is hereby formed, and the Partnership Agreement dated [DATE] is ratified and adopted; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the General Partner subscribes for the capital contribution fixed in Schedule A; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the principal establishment in Quebec is fixed at [ADDRESS], City of Montreal, Québec, Canada; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the General Partner is authorized to file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to pay all registration fees; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that [NAME] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [NAME] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and remit GST/QST; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that all officers may complete annual statutory declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online name search and reservation portal (Centre de recherche en ligne sur les entreprises du Québec).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a distinctive-name search against the REQ Central Registry to confirm the proposed partnership name (e.g., 'Custom Trust & Corporate Institute, S.E.C.') is not confusing with an existing enterprise and lawfully presentable in French. Optionally file an application for name reservation for up to 90 days; alternatively, retain a legal opinion on distinctiveness to support the declaration.
required_dossiers: Three proposed partnership names in order of preference
Legal opinion on distinctiveness (optional)
Application for name reservation (requête en réservation de nom), if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ refuses the name, correct the distinctive element indicated in the refusal notice, resubmit a modified name, or file a substantiated legal opinion; re-file within the correction window of the notice to avoid loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Registration Data Package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Drafting counsel acting on the authority of the General Partner.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) defining the general and limited partners' contributions, profit-sharing ratios, withdrawal rights, and exclusive management by the general partner. Prepare the Declaration of Registration data set: partnership name, head office, principal establishment in Quebec, and identity of the general partner (individual identity or corporate NEQ); limited partners need not be disclosed under art. 27 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Schedule of capital contributions and contribution receipts
General partner identification file (NEQ, Quebec address, jurisdiction of formation)
Power of attorney for the signatory, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a corporate general partner has no Quebec NEQ, first register that entity with REQ or provide proof of existing registration elsewhere in Canada; then re-submit the corrected data package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Declaration of Registration and Payment of Registration Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Services en ligne (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online services portal and submit the déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite, including the head office address in Quebec and general partner particulars; pay the online registration duty of CAD 50 (approx. USD 37). Upon validation, REQ issues the enterprise number (NEQ) immediately and later transmits the attestation of registration.
required_dossiers: New enterprise registration form data set
Proof of payment (online credit card or Interac)
Electronic signature of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ flags data-capture errors, correct the highlighted fields and re-submit; if errors are discovered after issuance, file a declaration of modification (déclaration modificative); late-filing penalties may be reduced upon proof of due diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Revenu Québec for GST/HST, QST and Employer Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Agence du revenu du Québec) — Entreprises online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the partnership NEQ, register for the federal GST/HST (5%) and the Quebec Sales Tax – QST (9.975%) on taxable supplies of the AI/LLM API platform; the general partner must obtain a persona number for the partnership and report pass-through income on the RL-15/RL-16 slips. Register as an employer only when hiring Quebec employees, in which case open payroll deduction accounts and register the establishment with CNESST.
required_dossiers: REQ enterprise number (NEQ)
Description of taxable supplies (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511)
Partnership legal name, trading name and business address
Bank account details of the partnership
Identification of the general partner and authorized representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec requests clarification of the registration, respond within the prescribed delay with the attestation of registration and an extract of the partnership agreement; voluntary disclosure may waive late-registration penalties in the absence of formal investigation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Adoption, Partnership Bank Account Onboarding and Compliance Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner, assisted by the corporate services provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a formal meeting of the general partner, adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, and open a Canadian partnership bank account under the partnership name with the suffix 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. File the annual update declaration (déclaration annuelle de mise à jour) with REQ each anniversary and maintain the partnership records, minutes, and capital allocation schedules in Quebec.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of registration (certificat d'attestation)
Executed First Board Resolution
Partnership agreement with contribution schedules
Beneficial ownership declarations of each partner (bank CIP)
Identification documents of general partner and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the application, provide the REQ attestation, partnership agreement, and a beneficial-ownership declaration; if onboarding remains blocked, apply to another Schedule I chartered bank or a provincial trust company with the same dossier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec (MEIE) — no industrial or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 6201 (software and LLM inference API services); MEIE only administers investment and innovation incentive programs for AI enterprises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. No provincial manufacturing or industrial operating licence is mandated for a pure AI/LLM API platform. A municipal business permit (permis d'affaires) may be required if the partnership leases office premises, issued by the relevant city or borough (e.g., Ville de Montréal) under its general by-laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Québec.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category IV. The activity consists solely of digital software services (generative AI and LLM inference APIs) with no fixed installation, industrial plant, or physical works; no full environmental impact assessment or authorization under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital activity. For leased offices or data-centre space, the operator must comply with municipal sewer and wastewater by-laws, electronic waste recovery under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (CQLR c Q-2, r. 42.1), and personal information protection obligations under the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Code (CQLR c B-1.1, r. 10): landlords must provide fire-safety conformity certificates for leased premises; structural-load inspections apply only to constructed facilities, not to service-tenancy software operations. Under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), the general partner must maintain a workplace risk assessment, first-aid kit, and CNESST establishment registration once five or more workers are employed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html); Revenu Québec — CliquezAffaires business registration portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/registering-your-business/) and Registraire des entreprises du Québec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine nexus. A limited partnership formed in Québec or an extra-provincial LP carrying on business in Québec must register with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Civil Code of Québec arts. 2188-2236) to obtain the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Step 2: Register for federal income tax and program accounts. Obtain the CRA 9-digit Business Number (BN) and register the RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll) and RC (corporation income tax, if applicable) accounts via Business Registration Online or Form RC1 / RC391 (for non-residents). Step 3: In Québec, Revenu Québec co-administers the GST/HST; the registrant must therefore also register with Revenu Québec for the GST/HST, the QST (Form LM-1, via CliquezAffaires), and provincial source deductions. Step 4: Obtain the QST registration certificate referencing the NEQ and BN. Step 5: Foreign non-resident partners must supply identity, residential and beneficial-ownership documentation; a non-resident partner without Canadian residence may be required to appoint a representative (Income Tax Act s. 273; Excise Tax Act s. 294.3) for service of process and compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada) s. 96 and the Taxation Act (Québec) ss. 599-600, a limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax: the LP is not a taxpayer and all income, gains, losses, tax credits and capital are computed at partnership level and allocated to partners. Non-resident partners are taxable on their Canadian-source share and may be subject to Part XIII withholding on distributions (treaty-reducible). For GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership is treated as a distinct 'person' / registrant in its own name. Québec is a civil-law jurisdiction for private law, but Canadian income tax and indirect tax legislation apply federally and provincially in a harmonized manner.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; transparency is statutory. Available elections include: (1) Income Tax Act s. 216 election by a non-resident partner to file a return on net Canadian-source rental income; (2) s. 216.1 deemed-dividend election converting non-resident partner allocations into dividends; (3) s. 96(1.1) and 96(6) partnership allocation designations for hybrid-mismatch alignment; (4) s. 156 GST/HST election for closely related corporations/partnerships to treat taxable supplies as made for nil consideration; (5) corresponding QST nil-consideration election under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax; (6) hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act Part 3.3 (ss. 18.4, 20.4, 91.7) addressing reverse hybrids and imported mismatches; and (7) irrevocable GST/HST registration election to accelerate registration ahead of the small-supplier threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered in Québec by Revenu Québec, plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax); combined headline rate = 5% GST + 9.975% QST = 14.975%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (Excise Tax Act s. 148; Quebec Sales Tax Act s. 28): a person ceases to be a small supplier once worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies but excluding financial services, capital property and goodwill, exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. For the AI/LLM API platform, monthly recurring token-based API fees count as taxable supplies for the threshold. Non-resident digital-supplier simplified rules (ETA Division IV.1) impose registration with no threshold in respect of Canadian consumers, but an LP carrying on business through a Québec permanent establishment follows the ordinary regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec operate a post-audit fiscal model with no real-time clearance, no government fiscal stamp, and no API-based stamping mandate. E-invoicing is permitted (PDF, XML, EDI, Peppol-based formats) provided the invoice is legible and contains the prescribed information: supplier legal name (the LP, not the partners), registration number for GST/HST and QST, date of invoice, description of the supply, consideration, and tax amounts. The CRA accepts structured electronic invoices, and Canada is progressively adopting the Pan-Canadian e-Invoice Interoperability Framework based on Peppol on a voluntary basis; business-to-government e-invoicing was launched in 2024-2025 but remains voluntary. Québec requires that a QST-registered supplier show its QST number on invoices and retain electronic books and records in conformity with the Regulation respecting books and records. No digital clearance or nightly validation is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 6 of the Excise Tax Act where goods are exported by the supplier or delivered to a carrier for direct export, supported by satisfactory evidence of export. Services and intangibles: a supply of a service or a supply of intangible personal property (including access to an AI/LLM inference engine, model weights, or API token rights) made to a non-resident person is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 7 and 10, provided the non-resident recipient is not registered for GST/HST and the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance. The QST zero-rating rules (Act respecting the Quebec sales tax and its regulations) are substantially harmonized with the GST. An AI API token supply qualifies as an exported intangible/service when the customer is a non-resident non-registrant and the platform does not or cannot reasonably determine that the supply is acquired for consumption or use in Canada. The supplier should obtain destination-based evidence (customer address, IP/geolocation, contract terms, payment origin) to support non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System / eManifest G12) for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Cargo Control Document) evidencing physical export and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 / payment confirmation) evidencing cross-border FX repatriation
Signed non-resident declaration from the customer confirming non-registrant status and non-Canadian use of the AI API services
Service or licensing agreement with the non-resident counterparty describing the supply, place of supply, and payment terms
Electronic usage and billing records (ticket-level token consumption, metering logs, IP geolocation) substantiating that the digital service was rendered to the non-resident
Corporate register extracts or beneficial ownership evidence for non-resident partners where the LP is claiming zero-rating on internal partner supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no codified 180-day FX repatriation deadline for services; the 180-day parameter reflects the administrative benchmark used by CRA and Revenu Québec for producing bank-repatriation evidence during audit. Penalties on fraudulent or undocumented export zero-rating: (1) reassessment of the full 14.975% combined GST/HST+QST retroactively where the supplier fails to sustain the non-resident or export documentation burden; (2) gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the tax sought to be evaded (Excise Tax Act s. 285.1); (3) false-statement penalty and failure-to-file penalties (ETA ss. 281.1, 280); (4) corresponding QST penalties under the Quebec Sales Tax Act, including 25% gross-negligence penalties and penal fines; (5) criminal prosecution for evasion (ETA s. 327) punishable by fines of 50%-200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years; (6) interest compounded daily on all reassessed amounts; and (7) the normal 6-year reassessment limitation period is waived where misrepresentation is attributable to fraud, neglect, or wilful default (ETA s. 298(1)(d)). Records and zero-rating support must be retained for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); Canada does not maintain a dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration, and exchange control supervision is instead effected through banking prudential rules, AML/ATF regulations, and sanctions administration administered by Global Affairs Canada and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has full currency convertibility under both current and capital account classifications, consistent with Article VIII of the International Monetary Fund Articles of Agreement. There are no statutory exchange controls, no mandatory conversion quotas, and no Central Bank approval obligation for profit repatriation by non-residents. The practical legal hurdles for a Quebec limited partnership distributing income to foreign partners are: (i) Canadian withholding tax on Part XIII payments where the income is sourced in Canada; (ii) FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting for amounts at or above CAD 10,000; (iii) OFSI consolidated sanctions list and SEMA compliance screening; (iv) business number registration and GST/HST administration obligations if the LP is carrying on business in Quebec; and (v) documentation evidencing entitlement under the applicable tax treaty to reduce withholding on service fees or royalties. For USDC and other crypto-asset receipt flows, the Financial Action Task Force-based AML rules require source-of-crypto wallet verification and the maintaining of blockchain forensic records where convertible virtual currency receipts form part of operating turnover.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, no minimum conversion ratios, and no time-limited repatriation obligations for software/cloud API export receipts under Canadian law. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency-denominated bank accounts held at any Schedule I Canadian bank, or in an offshore account subject to Canadian tax reporting on specified foreign property and attribution of foreign exchange gains or losses to the LP's partners for income tax purposes. Physical import or export of currency or bearer monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more triggers Form E311 (Cross-Border Currency or Monetary Instrument Report) to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Electronic inbound and outbound wire transfers attributable to the LP of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by the responsible financial intermediary to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Escrow Operation Multi-Currency Account (CAD, USD, EUR) for LP capital contributions and operational disbursements
Commercial Operating Account with Foreign Currency Sub-Accounts and Direct SWIFT Corporate Channel
Corporate Account for Treasury Services, with FX Convert and Zero-Balance Structure
Cash Management Operating Account and Merchant Processing Account
Non-Resident Business Account for Limited Partnership Treasury Flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for using offshore fintech EMIs is 'Medium' with legal constraints. Platforms such as Stripe Treasury, Wise Business, Airwallex and Payoneer can provide payment acceptance and foreign currency collection in Canada without being chartered banks, but they cannot legally serve as the sole repository for partner capital contributions or substantive treasury liquidity unless operated as registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs) in Canada under FINTRAC and holding provincial authority in Quebec. Large-value cross-border clearing above CAD 500,000 should exclusively use a Schedule I bank to avoid regulatory uncertainty, sub-custody risk, and PCMLTFA non-compliance. Incoming funds to an EMI may also create double KYC requirements and possible exposure to the unwinding of bank partner relationships. For low-value AI API subscription collections, Stripe as a payment facilitator is viable; for USDC treasury operations, a regulated custodian with Canadian MSB or provincial licensing must be engaged, and the LP should maintain the majority of operating cash in a Tier 1 Canadian bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not mandated by federal statute for a Quebec limited partnership opening a corporate bank account, but in substance the major Canadian clearing banks apply a risk-based due diligence policy that requires at least one senior representative of the corporate general partner to complete an in-person initial compliance interview at a main branch in Quebec or to provide a notarized remote interview package witnessed by an authorized notary within a FINTRAC-recognized jurisdiction. Where any limited partner is a non-resident legal entity with ownership greater than 25%, enhanced due diligence will ordinarily require a video conference call with the beneficial owner, legal counsel opinion letters, and certified corporate registries. In practice, a fully remote opening without any physical touchpoint is possible only where (i) the LP has an existing relationship with the same banking group, (ii) funds are sourced from a pre-verified Canadian or US financial institution, and (iii) the general partner is a regulated professional or licensed entity. For capital margin and escrow accounts, physical attendance or an equivalent notarized video assent is effectively mandatory to satisfy the bank's internal policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a chain containing a foreign limited partnership or trust: the bank cannot determine the natural-person owner of more than 25% of the LP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The following constitutes a complete filing: (1) executed limited partnership agreement and all side letters; (2) certificate of registration from Quebec Registraire des entreprises; (3) a Canadian counsel legal opinion confirming each partner's legal status; (4) register of direct and indirect partners with names, addresses, and proportionate capital commitments; (5) FATCA, CRS, and Canada Part XIII self-certification forms for every non-resident partner; (6) sanctioned-party screening results from a recognized commercial database; and (7) latest annual financial statements or capital contribution proof from the original funding institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of initial capital contribution from a jurisdiction on the FATF high-risk-monitored list or from an unregulated crypto-asset exchange.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The required defense bundle includes: (1) a source-of-wealth statement signed by the contributing limited partner and corroborated by bank statements of the originating institution; (2) chain-of-title documentation for crypto origin, including blockchain analytics report demonstrating wallet behavior and no exposure to darknet or mixers; (3) confirmation that the digital asset exchange holds a FINTRAC MSB registration or an equivalent supervisory registration; (4) valuation report on the in-kind contribution if capital is settled with USDC or other digital assets; and (5) indemnity and attestation under the Quebec Civil Code confirming capital has not been obtained by an offence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors, officers, or authorized signatories appearing on the account mandate with no Canadian identity or payroll footprint, triggering adverse media and PEP risk flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Satisfactory defense comprises: (1) valid passports or recognized national identity documentation for each signatory; (2) professional reference letters from a regulated DFS or lawyer with a minimum 5-year relationship; (3) notarized proof of business address and employment; (4) negative PEP screening report; (5) certified translation of any non-English company filings; and (6) a dedicated resolution from the LP's general partner limiting account signing authority to two-person limits and specifying the scope of permitted transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description mismatch: declared 'AI API platform' combined with high-frequency incoming payments from unrelated merchants or token traffic, simulating a payment intermediary or money laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank should receive: (1) a detailed business white paper explaining token consumption, pricing in API billings, and absence of third-party payment processing; (2) the executed master SaaS License Agreement and API Terms of Use; (3) a list of three to five enterprise customers with executed subscription agreements; (4) rolling invoice-level reporting showing revenue is compensation for computational capacity and model inference, not pass-through settlement; (5) data localization policy evidencing compliance with Quebec Bill 64 and PIPEDA; and (6) independent audit/security certification such as SOC 2 Type II to verify the bona fide operation of the technological platform.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital injections into the Quebec LP must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 pain.001 corporate-to-bank message through the originating bank and settled via the Canadian Lynx RTGS or correspondent US Fedwire network. The remittance field (field 70) must contain an unambiguous purpose descriptor, for example: 'LP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION // FDI // ISIC 6201 // AI LLM API PLATFORM // PROJECT [REF] // QUEBEC CA'. For each inbound transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, the receiving bank is required to file a FINTRAC International Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFT). The beneficiary must match the LP name and account mandate exactly; pre-delivery verification includes the payment confirmation, the partner's passport or entity registry, and a copy of the capital call notice issued by the general partner. Statistics Canada may require a Foreign Direct Investment Return if the cumulative Canadian-based assets or revenue exceed established thresholds; prompt response is necessary to avoid administrative penalties. To maximize clearance speed, inbound wires should use the intermediary bank specified by the receiving Schedule I bank and avoid multiple correspondent hops.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border operating payables for AI infrastructure, cloud computing, GPU capacity, data licensing, and professional services will settle through SWIFT MT103 for single payment instructions, SWIFT MT101 for direct debit origination to a treasury provider, or commercial letter of credit under UCP600 for large capital equipment or multi-year infrastructure contracts. For domestic Canadian disbursements, Payments Canada operating rails are the Lynx Real-Time Gross Settlement System for individual values above CAD 250,000, the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch transfers below CAD 25 million, and the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for lower-value immediate payments. Vendor payments requiring US dollar clearing outside Canada will use the US correspondent network or a bank-to-bank SWIFT gpi track. For each outgoing transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, the bank reports the transaction to FINTRAC, and for sanctions compliance, the beneficiary must be screened against the Specially Designated Nationals list and Canadian OFSI regulations prior to release. Crypto-asset disbursements should be limited to confirmed vendor arrangements and cleared via the LP's regulated digital-asset banking channel, with a fiat override always available to meet bank mandates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: plain vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with a Schedule I Canadian bank for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP, maturing up to 24 months, with ISDA 1998 FX and 2021 definitions.
FX swaps and cross-currency basis swaps involving CAD and USD concluded under a credit support annex of a standard ISDA Master Agreement with a licensed Canadian securities dealer.

European-style over-the-counter currency options (call or put) on CAD/USD for hedging revenue exposure; premiums paid from the operating account and physical settlement permitted for trade-related positions.

non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for hedging secondary exposures to emerging-market currencies where a onshore forward deliverable market is unavailable, and must never be used as a speculative or uncovered trade for a pass-through entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the period beginning 60 days before the registration anniversary and ending on the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an additional administrative duty and penalties of up to CAD 500 (approx. USD 370). REQ issues a formal notice of default; failure to remedy may lead to publication of a notice of intention to cancel the registration. Cancellation causes the limited partnership to lose the benefit of the legal publicity regime and may erode limited partners' liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (Form T5013) and T5013 Summary, including allocation of income, losses, and capital gains to partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year fiscal period ending December 31, due by May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of at least CAD 100 per month per return up to a maximum of CAD 500 per partner or CAD 2,500 for larger partnerships, plus possible gross-negligence penalties and criminal sanctions for wilful failure to file.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory mandatory audit for a limited partnership under Quebec civil law or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A certified audit is required only if imposed by the partnership agreement, by a creditor or investor, by securities regulators for a reporting issuer, or by specific financial-sector statutes. CRA may request complete financial statements (not necessarily audited) on audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), at the entity's choice; IFRS is required if the limited partnership consolidates into a public-company parent or is itself a reporting issuer.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for limited partnerships. Beneficial ownership information is captured through the annual updating declaration filed with REQ, which identifies general partners and limited partners. Any transfer or admission of a limited partner must be reported to REQ within 30 days of the change, and the internal register of partners must be updated accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited), containing contributions and transfers
Copy of the initial declaration and all updates filed with REQ
Books of account and supporting vouchers
Minute book containing limited partnership resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–15,000 depending on transaction volume, documentation depth, and AI-platform revenue complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal and Quebec corporate rate; LP is pass-through, partners taxed at individual rates)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credits, Quebec innovation tax credits, and small business deduction (if applicable to partners)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) via CRA's My Electronic Account or NETWOR
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name and Canadian business number (BN) if applicable; non-resident partners must be identified with their foreign tax ID.
Use the partnership's fiscal year-end; non-resident partners must align with this date for reporting.
Allocate income based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners must report their share in their home jurisdiction.
Report all income and deductible expenses; non-resident partners must ensure expenses are allocated correctly.
Non-resident partners must use this figure for their own tax filings and any withholding obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500; additional penalties for failure to provide information or for false statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 (Relevé de renseignements des sociétés de personnes) via Revenu Québec's Cliquez sur le service
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership identification (name, address, Quebec enterprise number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) if registered; non-resident partners must be listed with their foreign addresses.
Indicate the fiscal year-end; non-resident partners must align with this period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income or loss to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate according to the partnership agreement; non-resident partners must report their share to Revenu Québec if they have Canadian-source income.
Provide each partner's name, address, and share percentage; non-resident partners must provide their tax identification number.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500; plus interest on any unpaid amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (statutory for non-resident partners on allocated income; treaty may reduce)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) to the partnership to claim treaty relief; the partnership must withhold at the reduced rate if TRC is provided before the distribution or allocation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates typically 10% for royalties and 10% for interest (e.g., US treaty).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 5 million in aggregate transactions with non-residents (or if the partnership is a large entity with gross revenue/assets exceeding CAD 50 million)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have ESR, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply; partnerships must have real economic activity to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false statements, or fraudulent misrepresentation in tax filings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and interest on unpaid taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors (general partners) may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they fail to withhold or remit; civil restitution and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LP as a shell without economic substance, artificial transactions to avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, penalties up to 50% of tax avoided, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be personally liable for the tax liability if the partnership is deemed a sham; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with AML regulations, such as inadequate KYC, reporting suspicious transactions, or record-keeping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 2 million for corporations, imprisonment for individuals, and suspension of operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for AML violations if they knowingly participate or fail to supervise; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or pricing transactions not at arm's length, resulting in income adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 10% of the net adjustment, plus interest; potential double taxation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable if they knowingly participate in transfer pricing mispricing; civil penalties and potential criminal prosecution for gross negligence.
